title: Two-level PE Wells
subtitle: PE likelihood and investigation pathway
typeLabel: Investigation pathway — not a rule-out score
summary: Two-level PE Wells categorises suspected pulmonary embolism as likely or unlikely and directs the required investigation pathway.
population: People in whom pulmonary embolism remains clinically suspected.

criteria.label: Clinical signs and symptoms of DVT
An alternative diagnosis is less likely than PE
Immobilisation for at least 3 days or surgery in previous 4 weeks
Malignancy: treatment within 6 months or palliative

results.label: PE unlikely
interpretation: D-dimer is generally required unless PERC has already validly ruled out PE.
actions: Order D-dimer (high-sensitivity assay preferred, e.g., high-sensitivity ELISA); or assess PERC applicability (very low pre-test probability + credible alternative diagnosis)
If PERC criteria met and negative: discharge with PE red-flag counseling (sudden breathlessness, chest pain, syncope, leg swelling); arrange follow-up
If D-dimer negative: discharge with PE red-flag counseling and alternative diagnosis management plan
If D-dimer positive or PERC not applicable: proceed to CTPA or ventilation/perfusion imaging

results.label: PE likely
actions: Proceed directly to computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) or ventilation/perfusion imaging per institutional protocol; admit for imaging and monitoring

Initiate parenteral anticoagulation immediately if imaging is delayed (unfractionated heparin or low-molecular-weight heparin per local guidance); senior clinician review; arrange intensive-care bed if high-risk features (haemodynamic instability, right-ventricular strain)

overrides: Both categories require the appropriate D-dimer or imaging pathway.
limitations: The Wells score does not exclude PE by itself. Do not use it to justify scene discharge without completing the required pathway.

parityCases.description: Executable case for result band: PE unlikely.
Executable case for result band: PE likely.
All criteria set to their highest scoring values.
